seo.title: ODDfest — Helsinki's open creative platform
seo.description: A distributed, open creative platform across Helsinki — independent creators, collectives, venues and organisations hosting programme under one shared umbrella.

title: Helsinki's open creative platform.
intro: ODDfest is an open, distributed creative platform across Helsinki — independent artists, collectives, venues and organisations hosting their own programme under one shared identity, the same model Creative Week ran in 2026, opened up further for 2027.

features.title: Art & Performance
features.body: Installations, live shows and everything in between, hosted by independent venues and organisers across the city.

features.title: Club Culture
features.body: Club nights hosted by independent collectives and venues, all part of the same shared ODDfest week.

features.title: Collective Creation
features.body: Open calls, co-created works and space for anyone with something to bring, not just established names.

whatItIs.headline: An open platform, not a booked showcase.
whatItIs.body: Independent creators, collectives, venues, organisations, communities and companies create and host their own programme, and ODD connects it under one shared identity. Instead of producing every event centrally, ODD provides the platform, the visibility and the connections that make a distributed programme read as one shared moment.

howItWorks.title: Create or host something
howItWorks.body: Register your event, show, night or project as part of ODDfest — you keep full control of what you make and how.

howItWorks.title: Join the shared programme
howItWorks.body: Once confirmed, your programme appears in the shared ODDfest listing alongside everyone else's.

howItWorks.title: ODD connects and amplifies
howItWorks.body: ODD promotes the programme as a whole, and connects organisers to partners, audiences and each other.

howItWorks.title: Helsinki experiences it together
howItWorks.body: For one week, dozens of independent events read as a single citywide moment — Helsinki's creative scene, visible together.

organiserOwnership.headline: Your programme stays yours.
organiserOwnership.body: Taking part in ODDfest doesn't mean handing your event over. You keep creative control, your own budget and your own relationships — ODD's role is to connect what you're doing to a bigger shared platform, not to run it for you. The exact terms of participation for 2027 are still being finalised.

openCall.headline: Want to host something at ODDfest 2027?
openCall.body: The exact registration process, dates and deadlines are still being confirmed. Register your interest now and we'll tell you as soon as it opens.

forPartners.headline: Partner with the platform.
forPartners.body: Organisations that want to sponsor, host space for, or otherwise back the distributed ODDfest programme can partner with the platform as a whole rather than a single event.

previousEdition.title: The model this builds on.
previousEdition.body: In 2026, ODDfest ran as part of a wider Creative Week (June 8–14) — with ODDference on June 11–12 and ODDfest's own core programme on June 12–13, across venues including Lasipalatsi, Kulttuurikasarmi, Tavastia Club and more. ODDfest 2027 builds on that same distributed spirit, opened up further to more independent organisers across the city.

faq.question: Can I attend without pre-registering?
faq.answer: Most ODDfest programme is open to the public — check each event's own listing for specifics once the 2027 programme goes live.

faq.question: How do I host something at ODDfest?
faq.answer: Register your interest above. Once the 2027 registration process is confirmed, we'll be in touch with next steps and your event joins the shared programme.

faq.question: Is there one ticket for all of ODDfest?
faq.answer: No — ODDfest is a distributed programme, so ticketing (where it exists at all) is set by each individual host, not centrally by ODD.

faq.question: Is ODDfest accessible?
faq.answer: Accessibility varies by venue and host, since programme is organised independently across the city — check with individual organisers, or contact us if you need help finding accessible options.
